chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, raising it (mursal), he said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his which he delivered as a sermon upon the pulpit: O you people!

When you know, then act according to what you have known so that you may be guided. Indeed, the scholar who acts contrary to his knowledge is like the confused ignorant one who has not awakened from his ignorance. Nay, I have indeed considered that the argument against him is greater, and the regret is more prolonged for this scholar who has stripped himself away from his knowledge, compared to this bewildered ignorant one who is confused in his own ignorance — and both of them are confused, perishing.

Do not be suspicious lest you become doubtful, and do not doubt lest you fall into disbelief; do not grant yourselves concessions lest you become lax, and do not be lax with the Truth lest you incur loss. It is part of the Truth that you acquire religious understanding, and it is part of understanding that you not be deceived. Truly, the most sincere among you to himself is the most obedient to his Lord, and the most treacherous among you to himself is the most disobedient to his Lord. Whoever obeys God will be secure and receive glad tidings, and whoever disobeys God will be disappointed and will regret.

key_terms.الْعَالِمُ الْمُنْسَلِخُ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ: The scholar who has stripped himself of his knowledge — one who has knowledge but does not act on it, effectively abandoning it
key_terms.الْفِقْهُ: Deep religious understanding and jurisprudence — not just surface-level memorization but genuine comprehension that guards against self-deception
key_terms.الْمُدَاهَنَةُ: Compromise/laxity with the truth — a severe spiritual failing condemned in Islamic ethics
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Raising it (mursal/marfu') — a technical term indicating the chain does not fully reach the Prophet or Imam but is attributed to one by a narrator

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about scholars who do not act on their knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon from the pulpit, addressing the Muslim community on the critical relationship between knowledge and action. He warns that a scholar who does not act on his knowledge is actually in a worse position than an ignorant person, because the scholar's accountability before God is greater. The sermon then lays out a chain of spiritual decline — from suspicion to doubt to disbelief — and emphasizes that sincere advice to oneself is measured by obedience to God.
word_analysis: for you will fall into disbelief

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in a speech of his<sup>asws</sup> which he<sup>asws</sup> addressed in a sermon upon the Pulpit: ‘O you people!

When you know so act upon what you know so that you may be guided. A scholar acting with other than it (knowledge) is like the ignorant confused one who has not woken up from his ignorance. But, you will see that the argument against him is greater, and the regret would be more prolonged upon this scholar, the one alienated from his own knowledge than it would be upon this ignorant one, the one confused in his own ignorance, and both of them are confused, wandering.

Do not be suspicious, for you will be doubting, and do not doubt, for you would be disbelieving, and do not let go of yourselves for you would be lethargic (exhausted), and do not be lethargic with regards to the Truth, for you would be incurring loss. And it is from the Truth that you should be (acquiring) understanding, and it is from the understanding that you should not be deceived; and that the most advising to his own self is the one most obedient to his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and the most overwhelmed to his own self is the one most disobedient to his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. And the one who obeys Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would be secure and would receive glad tidings, and the one who disobeys Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, would lose out and regret’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father in a marfu‘ manner (rafa’ahu) from Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) who has said the following. “Once Imam Ali (a.s.) said in one of his sermons, ‘O people,

if you learn and gain knowledge you must act accordingly so that you may have guidance. A learned person who disregards his knowledge is like a lost and ignorant person who never comes to the right path due to his ignorance. In fact, you will find the case against such the learned that disregards his knowledge more sever and his regret more prolonged, compared to the ignorant person who wonders about in it. Both people stray and are devoid of goodness.

Do not hesitate lest you will doubt and do not doubt lest you will disbelieve. Do not be lenient to your souls to play lazy. Do not trivialize the truth lest you will lose badly. It is of the truth to learn Fiqh, proper understanding of religion. It is of Fiqh, proper understanding of religion not to suffer deceit. The wisest for ones self among you is the one most obedient to his Lord. The most deceitful to himself among you is the disobedient one to his Lord.
One who obeys Allah is safe and glad news awaits him but one who disobeys his Allah he loses and regrets.’”
